papers.title: Spectral Dynamics and Fuglede--Kadison Determinants for Wreath Products
papers.abstract: We investigate connections between operator spectra, complex dynamics, and determinants for wreath product groups. For a nontrivial finite abelian group $G$, the natural action of $G\wr\mathbb Z$ on a rooted tree produces a family of operators with a recursive structure. Applying Schur complements to this family yields a rational map on complex projective space. We determine the projective spectrum--the parameter values for which the operator pencil fails to be invertible--as the union of the Julia set of this map and an explicitly described subset of its Fatou set. We also prove that the associated Koopman representation and the left regular representation are weakly equivalent and therefore give the same projective spectrum. We then compute Fuglede--Kadison determinants for a family of operators on more general wreath products. These formulas yield injective operators with zero determinant for wreath products $K\wr\mathbb Z$, where $K$ is a discrete group admitting a nontrivial projection $e\in\mathbb C[K]$. This answers negatively a question of Li and Thom about whether injectivity implies positive determinant for operators defined by matrices over complex group rings of amenable groups. For $G_{tf}\rtimes_\sigma\mathbb Z$, where $G_{tf}$ is any countable torsion-free abelian group and $\sigma\in\operatorname{Aut}(G_{tf})$, we prove that injectivity does imply positive determinant in every matrix size.

papers.title: Hyperrigidity and convexity in two variables
papers.abstract: We extend Brown's one-variable rigidity theorem to strictly convex functions of two variables under a regularity assumption. Let $K\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be nonempty, compact, and convex, and let $f$ be real-valued, strictly convex on $K$, and of class $C^2$ on a neighbourhood of $K$. We prove that the generating set $\{x_1,x_2,f\}$ is hyperrigid in $C(K)$.

papers.title: Pseudo-Fredholm operators form a regularity on Hilbert spaces
papers.abstract: Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space. We prove that the class of pseudo-Fredholm operators on $H$ is a regularity in the sense of Kordula and M\"uller. We also prove that the classes of left and right generalized Drazin invertible operators are regularities on $H$. Consequently, the generalized Kato spectrum and the corresponding generalized Drazin spectra satisfy the spectral mapping theorem. We construct an operator $T$ on a separable complex Banach space such that $T^2$ is right generalized Drazin invertible whereas $T$ is not pseudo-Fredholm. In particular, the power axiom need not hold for pseudo-Fredholm operators on Banach spaces. Finally, we show that the accumulation sets of the approximate point and surjectivity spectra define regularities on Banach spaces, yielding another proof of the regularity of generalized Drazin invertible operators in $\B(X)$.

papers.title: The e-Property for Quantum Markov Semigroups
papers.abstract: Let $(\mathcal{T}_t)_{t\geqslant0}$ be a quantum Markov semigroup on a von Neumann algebra and let $\mathcal{A}$ be an invariant Feller $C^*$-algebra. We formulate the $e$-property on the full state space and show that its quantitative defect is equivalent, within an optimal factor two, to the Hausdorff measure of non-compactness of observable orbits. We develop Ces\`aro and Lip-norm criteria and a generalised Doeblin minorisation by a state-space contracting positive map, including finite-dimensional and measure-prepare factorisations. When every observable has the $e$-property, the Jacobs--de Leeuw--Glicksberg decomposition identifies the reversible Choi--Effros algebra and the norm-stable sector. Expected and decoherence-free subalgebras transfer the property under norm decay of the complementary dynamics, including infinite-dimensional ultracontractive and finite-index Pimsner--Popa regimes. Finally, we establish the full comparison hierarchy among ordinary, eventual, Ces\`aro and pointwise eventual equicontinuity notions, reinforced by matrix Jamison and homoclinic flow counterexamples. Projection-face criteria are treated in a companion paper.

papers.title: Every classifiable simple C*-algebra has a C*-diagonal
papers.abstract: We construct C*-diagonals in all UCT Kirchberg algebras. Together with known constructions of C*-diagonals in the stably finite setting by Xin Li, this shows that every classifiable C*-algebra (in the sense of the Elliott classification programme) has a C*-diagonal. In fact, we show that every UCT Kirchberg algebra admits an untwisted principal \'etale groupoid model with a finite-dimensional unit space.

papers.title: Super McDuff and Uniformly Super McDuff $\rm II_1$ factor
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that every super McDuff $\rm II_1$ factor is uniformly super McDuff. In particular, the classes of super McDuff and uniformly super McDuff $\rm II_1$ factors coincide. This answers \cite[Question D]{GJKEP} affirmatively. For factors with separable predual, super McDuffness is therefore equivalent to the Brown property and is preserved under elementary equivalence, also answering \cite[Question~6.2.1]{AGK22} affirmatively. We further show that every infinite tensor product of non-$\Gamma$ $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors is uniformly super McDuff. For a finite tensor product of separable $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors that is super McDuff, each tensor factor is either non-$\Gamma$ or uniformly super McDuff, and at least one is uniformly super McDuff.

papers.title: The ultrapower $\mathcal R^\omega$ is not a group factor
papers.abstract: Let $(\mathcal M_n)_{n\geqslant 1}$ be a sequence of type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors with property $\Gamma$ and let $\omega$ be a free ultrafilter on $\mathbb N$. We prove that every subfactor of the ultraproduct $\prod_\omega\mathcal M_n$ of finite Jones index is not isomorphic to the group von Neumann algebra of any discrete group. In particular, the ultrapower $\mathcal R^\omega$ of the hyperfinite type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor $\mathcal R$ is not a group factor.

papers.title: Factoriality of Mixed $q$-Gaussian Algebras at the Boundary
papers.abstract: We determine the center and characterize factoriality for mixed $q$-Gaussian von Neumann algebras associated with real symmetric matrices $Q=(q_{ij})_{i,j\in I}$ satisfying $|q_{ij}|\le1$. We prove that every central element is supported on the singleton components of the strict graph of $Q$ and on its two-vertex components $\{a,b\}$ with $q_{aa}=q_{bb}=-1$ in terms of the graph-theoretic language. We also determine the spectral laws of some central elements.

papers.title: Unital qubit channels are $3$-noisy
papers.abstract: The algebraic and environmental characteristics of mixed unitary quantum operations are investigated. It is established that the composition of two uniformly n-mixed unitary channels is itself n-noisy, and this n-noisy property is shown to be an invariant under unitary equivalence. Furthermore, by utilizing majorization and the divisibility of Kraus rank-four unital qubit channels, we demonstrate that any unital qubit channel can be physically simulated using a three-dimensional maximally mixed environment. Together, these results advance the classification and physical realization of noisy quantum channels.

papers.title: Approximate Synthetic Spectra of Quantum Systems Associated with Compact Lie Groups
papers.abstract: How can noncommuting quantum observables retain the geometry of a classical phase space? Motivated by Mumford's question on approximately macroscopically unique (AMU) states and the work of Lin and Wang, we study synthetic spectra of position--momentum and angular-momentum systems. Under the hypotheses of their AMU theorems, nonempty synthetic spectra yield AMU states. For sufficiently small $\hbar$, the position--momentum spectrum fills the plane, while the angular-momentum spectrum contains any prescribed ball. The latter calculation leads to compact Lie groups: we prove that highest-weight coadjoint orbits lie in regional synthetic spectra under an explicit variance bound. Function-space representations of $SU(n)$, $SO(n)$, and $Sp(n)$ provide further examples.

papers.title: Noncommutative sharp Hausdorff-Young inequality
papers.abstract: We prove the sharp Hausdorff--Young inequality on quantum euclidean spaces. Our result implies the sharp Hausdorff--Young constants for the Weyl transform. The key ingredients are a sharp Hessian comparison inequality and a novel flow related to the mixed- norm of noncommutative Gabor transform; the Hessian comparison leads to the monotonicity of the flow. We also apply the same flow technique to prove the sharp Hausdorff--Young inequalities on Heisenberg groups and the affine group.

papers.title: Biexact von Neumann algebras
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of biexactness for general von Neumann algebras, naturally extending the notion from group theory. We show that biexactness implies solidity for von Neumann algebras, and that many of the examples of solid von Neumann algebras contained in the literature are, in fact, biexact. We also give examples of certain crossed products arising from Gaussian actions that are solid but not biexact, and we give examples of certain $q$-Gaussian von Neumann algebras that are strongly solid but not biexact. The techniques developed involve studying a certain weak form of nuclear embeddings, and we use this setting to give a new description of weak exactness for von Neumann algebras, which allows us to answer several open problems in the literature about weakly exact von Neumann algebras.

papers.title: Non-linear traces of Choquet type on AF algebras
papers.abstract: We study non-linear traces of Choquet type on unital AF algebras. Building on the matrix-algebra theory of Nagisa--Watatani and the UHF setting considered by Sogame, we first establish the corresponding description for finite direct sums of matrix algebras and then pass to arbitrary unital AF algebras. We prove that the cone of Choquet traces on an AF algebra $A$ is isomorphic, as an ordered cone, to the cone of increasing maps $\alpha:\Gamma(A)\to[0,\infty)$ satisfying $\alpha(0)=0$. On each finite-dimensional stage, the associated trace is given by an explicit Choquet formula involving spectral values and the classes of spectral projections.

papers.title: Geometric Aspects of $C^*$-Extreme Points II
papers.abstract: Building on the results of \cite{HR}, we investigate the relationship between \(C^*\)-extremality and linear extremality in the closed unit balls of general unital \(C^*\)-algebras. We show that, unlike in von Neumann algebras, these two notions of extremality need not coincide in general \(C^*\)-algebras. More precisely, we prove that the unilateral shift is a linear extreme point, but not a \(C^*\)-extreme point, of the closed unit ball of the Toeplitz \(C^*\)-algebra. We further establish that \(C^*\)-extremality implies linear extremality whenever the \(C^*\)-algebra admits a faithful unital representation on a separable Hilbert space. We also prove this implication for elements admitting a factorization $x=v|x|$, where $v$ is a partial isometry belonging to the algebra, and extend the result to suitable quotient \(C^*\)-algebras, including the Calkin algebra. Finally, we characterize the linear extreme points of the closed unit ball of unital \(C^*\)-subalgebras of \(B(H)\) containing the compact operators.
